ops.d: List every accounts in the subscription.
List the accounts in a resource group.

features.t: Accounts (create, get, list, update, delete) over ARM — every kind in core/azure_cognitiveservices_core.py KINDS

x: Keys are deterministic simulator secrets, not material an inference call is checked against — any non-empty bearer value is accepted by the (non-simulated) data plane. regenerateKey changes the stored value and is honest about which of Key1/Key2 it rotated.

features.t: Model deployments (create, get, list, delete) over ARM — Azure OpenAI and Azure AI services kinds
x: Deployment, quota and rate-limit bookkeeping (capacity, Tokens-Per-Minute quota per model) is real, and the deployment's data plane (chat/completions, completions, embeddings) is served by core/ai_models_core over the shared local-LLM seam: every deployment is answered by the same small local model, so the model name is not honoured.

Sends chat/completions to the deployment through the real Azure OpenAI wire; the answer comes from one small local model (llama.cpp on the appliance, WebLLM on Nano when the page registers it), so quality is toy-grade and no model running returns the native 503 ServiceUnavailable instead of an answer. No image/audio, function calling, 'On your data', content filters or fine-tuning.

features.t: Quotas (usages: per-model Tokens-Per-Minute for OpenAI/AIServices, TotalCalls for every other kind)
Networking (public network access / firewall default action)
x: publicNetworkAccess and networkAcls round-trip through ARM exactly as written, but Vyomi does not enforce them against the account's Keys and Endpoint or Model deployments calls — unlike azure.keyvaults.networking, this data plane has no per-account routing signal to check (no x-vyomi-account equivalent is wired into core/aws_wire_router.py for Microsoft.CognitiveServices yet).
System-assigned identity (principalId/tenantId) is real and persists across PATCH.

features.t: Resource locks (Microsoft.Authorization/locks), scoped to this account
x: Lock create/list/delete are real Microsoft.Authorization/locks over ARM at resource, resource-group and subscription scope (CanNotDelete/ReadOnly, name and notes validated); this blade manages the locks scoped to this Cognitive Services account only and has no scope switch. A resource-group or subscription lock really blocks writes and deletes of everything under it with 409 ScopeLocked (core/azure_arm_ext_core.py lock_conflict), but a lock set directly on a Cognitive Services account is stored and listed only: it does not block writes or deletes of the Cognitive Services account itself.

Only console/SDK-triggered mutations made since the simulation booted are recorded (no historical backfill), and `caller` is a fixed placeholder identity rather than the real signed-in principal. Severity/category filtering is not modelled (every recorded event is Informational/Administrative).

There is a fixed soft-delete retention window applied by the engine rather than a configurable per-account retention policy (Cognitive Services accounts have no 'purge protection' toggle in real Azure either, unlike Key vaults).

Check access, Role assignments and Deny assignments are REAL and scoped to this Cognitive Services account's resource id: Check access runs core/azure_iam_core.py's evaluator (explicit-deny-wins, scope inheritance from the subscription/resource group), the lists filter the shared RBAC store to assignments whose scope covers it, and new assignments are created scoped to it. Principal IDs are free text (Vyomi has no real directory); 'My access' and Classic administrators stay honest gaps. Update: the Deny assignments list, Classic administrators (a read-only list of the subscription's account administrator, like the real API) and My access (the simulated signed-in principal, evaluated with checkAccess) are now real shared tabs (azure.common.*); the gap wording above predates them.

A task is a REAL Microsoft.Logic/workflows record (Recurrence trigger + Http actions against management.azure.com) created from a template via POST .../Microsoft.Logic/vyomiCreateTask; runs are fired by the simulator scheduler (core/schedule_core.py) or 'Run now' and call the simulator's own ARM, so the effect is real (power state, restarts, key rotation, usage snapshots), with per-action results in Microsoft.Logic/workflows/runs. Only Recurrence triggers and Http-to-ARM/Compose actions run (anything else fails the run with ActionNotSupported); the managed identity is not authorised (RBAC is not evaluated); workflow expressions are not evaluated; there are no e-mail/Teams connectors, so report tasks keep their result in the run output. Missed schedules coalesce into one run; Nano only fires schedules while the tab is open.
